summary: Backend-only regression verification of the users.email redundant-index removal (idx_users_email dropped; users_email_key UNIQUE retained). Created /app/backend/tests/test_iter100_email_index_regression.py (20 pytest tests) covering DB index inventory, DB-level UNIQUE enforcement, planner index usability, login by email (admin/manager/jane + mixed-case + unknown-email 401), admin create-user duplicate/unique/mixed-case-duplicate, org invite-user duplicate/unique, admin update-user email change (unique / clash-rejected / same-value), and the full forgot-password -> reset-password -> login-with-new-password flow incl. mixed-case lookup. Result: 20/20 passed. Verified via pg_indexes that public.users now has only users_pkey, users_email_key (UNIQUE btree on email), idx_users_org_id, idx_users_team_id, idx_users_setting_id. No regressions found; all test data cleaned up.

minor.issue: `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_users_email;` is schema-unqualified. This DB (Supabase) also has an index literally named idx_users_email on auth.users; it survived here (verified still present), but the statement's target depends on the connection role's search_path. Should be `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.idx_users_email;` to be deterministic and to guarantee a Supabase-managed auth index can never be dropped.

Pre-existing/environmental: Resend rejects @example.com recipients ('Invalid `to` field'), logged as ERROR. Flow still returns 200 and the reset token is created (failure is caught), so functionally fine, but test-domain emails pollute error logs.

action_items: Optional hardening: qualify the drop as `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.idx_users_email;` in init_db.py schema patches.
critical_code_review_comments: init_db.py: unqualified DROP INDEX relies on search_path; auth.users.idx_users_email exists in this Supabase DB, so qualify with public. to eliminate any chance of dropping the wrong index.

Email uniqueness is enforced only by an application-level SELECT-then-INSERT (admin.create_user, org.invite_user) plus the DB UNIQUE constraint; the app path is racy but the constraint catches it — a concurrent duplicate would surface as an unhandled UniqueViolationError (500) rather than a clean 400. Consider catching asyncpg.UniqueViolationError and returning 400.

Email stored lowercased by writers, but some read paths use `email = $1` and others `LOWER(email)=LOWER($1)`; the latter cannot use users_email_key. Consider standardising on lowercased comparisons at write time only, or add a functional index if LOWER() lookups become hot.

success_rate.frontend: not tested (no frontend changes this round)

seed_data_creation: Temporary users test_iter100_*@example.com (create/invite/edit/reset fixtures) — all deleted in session teardown; verified zero residue. login_attempts/rate-limit rows cleared via tests/clear_rate_limit.py.

context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iter100_email_index_regression.py is a reusable regression suite for email flows. Note: /api/auth/forgot-password is IP-rate-limited to 5 requests / 15 min — run `python /app/backend/tests/clear_rate_limit.py` before re-running the suite or the last forgot-password test will 429 (this caused the only transient failure observed, not a product bug). pytest.ini auto-adds -n loadscope, so -p no:xdist is rejected.
rca_of_the_issue: idx_users_email was a plain btree duplicate of users_email_key (the UNIQUE constraint's index) on the same single column; Postgres never needed both. Dropping it removes write/maintenance overhead with zero read impact — all email equality lookups (login, forgot-password, uniqueness checks) are still served by users_email_key, confirmed by EXPLAIN with enable_seqscan=off.
